channel.title: Los Angeles Times - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from Los Angeles Times (latimes.com)

item.title: Judge blocks Trump administration move to cut $600 million in HIV funding from states
item.description: A federal judge granted California and other states a temporary restraining order halting the administration's health funding cuts for 14 days while the litigation continues.

item.title: Second video offers more clues in Nancy Guthrie abduction as authorities seek answers
item.description: The video, which was captured on a Ring camera about 1:54 a.m., shows a bald man wearing a gray jacket and a backpack similar to the one worn by the masked man outside Guthrie's door before she was abducted.

item.title: Rejecting science, Trump reverses conclusion that climate change is harming Americans
item.description: The 2009 endangerment finding affirms that carbon dioxide and other greenhouse gases pose a threat to human health and welfare. Its repeal marks one of the most significant deregulatory actions in U.S. history.

item.title: Six L.A. power players who found themselves in the Epstein files
item.description: The latest release of Epstein files shines new light on the disgraced financier's former relationships with several Los Angeles power players, including a prominent film director, a celebrity chef and an NFL owner.

item.title: UCLA professor's emails to Epstein stir protest as academia is jolted by links to sex abuser
item.description: Mark Tramo, a UCLA professor who researches the brain and music, faces criticism for his email exchanges with Jeffrey Epstein, including one supporting Epstein as he faced prostitution charges.

item.title: D4vd's family members are fighting grand jury subpoenas in the case of a dead teen found in the singer's car
item.description: The father, mother and brother of singer known as D4vd have tried to quash a subpoena to testify in California in the case of the teenager found in the singer's Tesla.

item.title: L.A. liable for destroying homeless people's property, federal judge rules
item.description: In a lawsuit over L.A.'s seizure of homeless people's belongings, a federal judge found the city modified or fabricated records in more than 100 camp cleanups, tainting the evidence so much that a fair trial was not possible. She ruled the city violated the Constitution and was liable for the lost personal property.

item.title: How Chipotle lost its sizzle
item.description: The Newport Beach-based Mexican chain Chipotle saw its same-store sales decline in 2025 for the first time since the company went public in 2006.

item.title: California launches civil rights probe into botched evacuations in historically Black Altadena
item.description: California Atty. Gen. Rob Bonta announced an investigation into potential civil rights violations during the emergency response to the Eaton fire. West Altadena, a historically Black community, received late evacuation alerts and few firefighting resources, The Times has reported.

item.title: Culver City, a crime haven? Bondi's jab falls flat with locals
item.description: Responding to Atty. Gen. Pam Bondi's jab, people who live or work in Culver City posted photos of clean streets, manicured parks and humming community events.
